gate_1_bounds_plant_reachable.claim: with the box fix in, the test fails on every run with the bounds plant (the root's bounds' derivative stopped) and on no run without it

prediction.value: 30 of 30 planted runs caught, 0 of 30 clean runs failed
prediction.basis: measured-before (20 of 20 before the fix) and derived: the plant removes the bounds' derivative, which every draw with an active bound shows against central differences; the fix makes every draw have one, so no draw can pass the plant by having no bound
prediction.why: a draw with no active bound previously failed the clean test on the premise assertion; planted, it failed on it too, so the old test also caught the plant on such draws (by the premise failing, not by the derivative); the fix removes the premise failure and tests the derivative on them. A plant that leaves a draw's derivative within 1e-6 of central differences would show as a missed run

control.plant: the bounds' derivative stopped (lax.stop_gradient on the slew box's low and high)

gate_1_bounds_plant_reachable.if_wrong: a miss or a clean failure stops this work and is reported with its seed; no tolerance or draw is loosened
gate_1_bounds_plant_reachable.cannot_discriminate_if: a planted run is inconclusive (a timeout or a crash counts against caught); Hypothesis stops on the first failing example, so a planted run's detection says the plant is visible on SOME draw of the 40, which is what 'fails every run' asks

gate_2_bounds_plant_unreachable.claim: the same on the unreachable id

prediction.value: 30 of 30 planted runs caught, 0 of 30 clean runs failed
prediction.basis: guess (never planted on this id on a runner); the mechanism is the same as gate 1's
prediction.why: unreachable targets leave rows unmet, but the box's bounds enter the solve identically; the derivative in the last joints passes through the active bound

gate_2_bounds_plant_unreachable.if_wrong: reported with seeds; this id is the one a miss would most likely be on, and would mean the bounds' derivative is not tested there, not that the fix failed

memory: each arm's largest process about 2.5 GiB (a fresh process of this test measured 2527 MiB); the estimator reads JAX programs, not tests, so probe/declared_peak.py declares a placeholder of that size (bound about 3.4 GiB) and says so
